subject: Chemistry
q: Match each oxide with its nature: (a) CO, (b) BaO, (c) Al₂O₃, (d) Cl₂O₇; (i) basic, (ii) neutral, (iii) acidic, (iv) amphoteric.
hint: Classify the metal and non-metal oxides separately.
solution: CO is neutral, BaO is basic, Al₂O₃ is amphoteric and Cl₂O₇ is acidic. Thus the matching is (a)-ii, (b)-i, (c)-iv, (d)-iii.

subject: Chemistry
q: Urea reacts with water to form a substance that decomposes to ammonia. When this gas is passed into aqueous Cu²⁺, a deep-blue solution forms. What is the complex ion in that solution?
hint: Excess ammonia forms a characteristic tetraammine complex with Cu²⁺.
solution: Hydrolysis ultimately supplies NH₃, which coordinates with Cu²⁺ to form the deep-blue tetraamminecopper(II) ion, [Cu(NH₃)₄]²⁺.

subject: Chemistry
q: Match: (a) CO(g) + H₂(g), (b) temporary hardness of water, (c) B₂H₆, (d) H₂O₂ with (i) Mg(HCO₃)₂ and Ca(HCO₃)₂, (ii) an electron-deficient hydride, (iii) synthesis gas, (iv) non-planar structure.
hint: Identify synthesis gas first, then the cause of temporary hardness.
solution: CO + H₂ is synthesis gas; bicarbonates of Ca and Mg cause temporary hardness; diborane is electron deficient; and H₂O₂ is non-planar. Hence (a)-iii, (b)-i, (c)-ii, (d)-iv.

subject: Chemistry
q: Which set contains only molecules with zero dipole moment?
hint: Look for symmetric molecular geometries whose bond dipoles cancel.
solution: BF₃ is trigonal planar, BeF₂ and CO₂ are linear, and para-dichlorobenzene is symmetric; their bond dipoles cancel. Each other set contains at least one polar molecule.
